articles.title: Dem candidate seized by Israeli forces while harvesting olives with Palestinians
articles.description: Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander was detained by Israeli troops in the West Bank while helping Palestinian farmers harvest olives, an Israeli rights group said. Lander, the former New York City comptroller, announced his detention Wednesday in a post on X that included a selfie taken aboard a bus. About 90 volunteers with Rabbis for Human Rights, an Israeli group, were detained near Nahalin, a village outside Bethlehem, the Jerusalem Post reported. A source told the Post that Lander was later released with a warning. “I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers. We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank,” Lander wrote. “The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know.” Lander won the Democratic nomination for New York’s 10th Congressional District in June, defeating Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY), PoliticsNY reported. He faces Republican Jennifer Moore in November, according to News 12. In a video posted by the group Israelis for Peace, Lander said, “They’ve just told us that all of the non-Israelis, all of the internationals who have been harvesting today, are gonna get on that bus. That is to say, we’re being arrested by the Israeli military for harvesting olives.” “We were not causing any problem or making any threats to anyone,” he said. “[Palestinians] haven’t harvested it since Oct. 7 because they’re afraid Israeli settlers will come and beat them or burn their olive trees.” Anton Goodman, acting executive director of Rabbis for Human Rights, said in a statement quoted by the Post, “We came to accompany farmers to land they had been unable to access for three years, and after two hours of peaceful olive harvesting, large numbers of troops arrived and closed off the area.” “Instead of protecting people working their land, the army is keeping them away from it and detaining those who came to accompany them for identification,” Goodman said. Troops declared the field a closed military zone, an area off-limits to civilians, the Post reported. Activists told the outlet they agreed to go but were detained anyway. Palestinian olive pickers were detained along with the activists, the Times of Israel reported, citing Palestinian media. Police took the foreign volunteers to a regional military headquarters for questioning, a source told the Post. One detainee told the outlet that no one was harmed. The Israel Defense Forces did not respond to the Post’s request for comment. Rabbi Jill Jacobs, CEO of the rabbinic human rights group T’ruah, and former Israeli Deputy Attorney General Yehoshua Schoffman were among those detained, the Post reported. Jacobs said in a statement that the military “forcibly removed those who came to provide a protective presence.” Gilad Kariv, a member of Israel’s parliament from the Democrats party, said that the group "did not break any laws or violate any lawful orders, nor did they confront anyone.” Israeli authorities are inclined to deport the foreign activists, a source told the Post.

articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy’s Disgusting Amy Acton Ad Blows Up in His Face
articles.description: Vivek Ramaswamy’s disgusting campaign advertisement featuring his opponent Amy Acton’s estranged mother is already backfiring. The Ohio GOP gubernatorial nominee’s team finally claimed credit Tuesday for an ugly attack ad featuring Donna Arthur, who lost custody of Acton after years of documented issues, including homelessness and sexual abuse by a stepfather. In the video, Arthur accused her daughter of lying about her upbringing. The video did not originally include any sponsors or political disclosures. Now Ramaswamy’s campaign is paying $4 million to stream the ad because it did well with “persuadable” voters, Axios reported. It’s a surprising move considering that the rhetoric was so far afield from responsible campaigning that even Republicans are recoiling. Meghan McCain slammed the “dastardly” ad, and Utah Senator Mike Lee’s longtime aide Dan Hauser publicly apologized for sharing it online. A Republican operative close to Ramaswamy’s campaign told Politico’s Playbook Wednesday: “It’s so gross to forsake family members for politics. I think it’s bad. It’s just morally bad.” Another senior GOP operative familiar with MAGA Inc.’s strategy told Playbook: “If Republicans are failing to lay out a reason to come vote for them and saying, ‘Here’s what I, as a candidate, am for, what I am going to do to make your economics better,’ there’s a good chance they’re going to lose.” Not only does the advertisement fail to deliver a closing argument, but more than anything, it serves to resurface Acton’s devastating family history and remind people why they hate Ramaswamy so much in the first place. The ad is reminiscent of his clash with former Republican presidential hopeful Nikki Haley, when he brought up her daughter during a debate. In response to his latest low blow, Haley said Tuesday: “He’s a bad guy. It’s a shame he continues to get away with it.” Acton’s campaign responded with its own advertisement Tuesday, in which her brother Philip Stearns discussed the abuse they experienced as children. “I experienced a lot of abuse, but Amy always got the worst of it,” he said. “Shame on Vivek. It’s the contempt he has for Amy. It’s the contempt he has for Ohio. He’s not fit to lead,” he added.

articles.title: Another Bush family member breaks ranks in Texas — and takes subtle jab at Trump
articles.description: Neil Bush, the younger brother of ex-President George W. Bush, says he cast his ballot for Democrat James Talarico over Republican Ken Paxton in Texas' U.S. Senate race, according to Newsweek. Bush, 71, the son of George H.W. Bush and head of his father’s Points of Light nonprofit, wrote in a Facebook post Tuesday that he’d voted early for Talarico. He said he’s been a Republican most of his life but that character outweighs party. He said he was deeply troubled by Paxton’s attempt as attorney general to challenge the 2020 results in other states in order to keep Donald Trump in power, which he called an assault on democratic institutions and the peaceful transfer of power. He added that his vote was “about much more” than Paxton. Though he has never met Talarico, he praised him as respectful, seeking common ground and interested in unifying people, with a faith that seems a source of humility. “Today, I voted against a style of politics that I believe has damaged our country,” Bush concluded. Most polls have Talarico narrowly ahead. Barbara Bush, George W. Bush’s daughter, reportedly gave $2,500 to a super PAC backing him. George W. Bush has mostly stayed quiet about Trump. Newsweek said it contacted both campaigns for comment. Trump has done everything in his power to try to boost Paxton, as well as Texas Republicans generally. He was the driving push behind last year's GOP mid-decade redistricting to make five congressional seats in Texas more Republican, though observers suggest that redraw may not be as successful as previously assumed.

articles.description: France is known for its vibrant protest culture, where activism is seen as a social duty and part of the national identity. From high fuel taxes to better pay for farmers, the French take to the streets with passion. Protests are considered a rite of passage for young people and a way to drive change beyond voting. articles.title: In midterm election, childcare costs are a factor for undecided voters
articles.description: Rising childcare costs are a factor for parents weighing how to vote in November's midterm elections. In Pennsylvania's hotly contested 7th Congressional District, both candidates are making childcare part of their pitch to voters. Democratic nominee Bob Brooks supports universal prekindergarten and increased federal childcare assistance. Republican Rep. Ryan Mackenzie, the incumbent, favors bigger tax breaks for families paying for childcare and employers who subsidize it for their workers. Childcare costs have rose faster than inflation from from 2020 to 2024. The Campaign for a Family Friendly Economy said it has spent $60 million this year to support Democratic candidates, who have historically favored bigger-ticket childcare investments.

articles.title: UNHCR Iran | From Macroeconomic Distress to Protection Risks: Economic Impacts of the 2026 Military Escalation on Afghans in Iran
articles.description: Please refer to the attached file. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 2026 military escalation in the Islamic Republic of Iran has intensified macroeconomic distress that can translate into serious protection risks for Afghan refugees and other Afghans in the country. The concern is not only direct exposure to hostilities but also how economic pressures can cascade through everyday life: rising prices, jobs, reduced access to public services, legal status and documentation challenges, higher healthcare costs, housing pressures and diminished household coping capacity, all of which can heighten protection risks. The evidence points to three interconnected ways in which these pressures are affecting Afghans in Iran. First, macroeconomic and labour-market pressures are weakening household incomes: inflation is eroding purchasing power, while employment loss, reduced working hours and unpaid wages are undermining livelihoods. Workers in the informal sector are particularly exposed to marginalization, exploitation and limited social protection. At the same time, rising housing costs and limited savings are reducing households’ ability to absorb shocks. Second, administrative and service-related pressures are creating additional protection risks: the costs and requirements associated with legal status, documentation renewal, health insurance and proof of residence can become increasingly difficult to meet, particularly for poorer households. Third, these pressures do not affect everyone equally. They can have a sharper impact on women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, female-headed households, people with chronic medical needs and undocumented or precariously documented Afghans, who may face greater barriers to accessing services, livelihoods and protection. The escalation did not create these vulnerabilities.¹ Rather, it has exposed, intensified and accelerated pressures that were already affecting Afghans in Iran, including sanctions-related macroeconomic stress, inflation, limited savings, informal employment, restricted legal and administrative access, healthcare affordability constraints, underfunded protection services and increasing pressure to return to Afghanistan. This distinction matters because the nature of these pressures calls for policy responses that go beyond emergency humanitarian assistance. In the immediate term, this includes preserving legal stay, protecting access to documentation and healthcare, supporting livelihoods, preventing returns under adverse circumstances, alongside strengthening resilient national and humanitarian systems. Over the longer-term, responses should address the underlying drivers of vulnerability by advancing the humanitarian-development-peace nexus and creating pathways toward durable solutions through greater socioeconomic inclusion and self-reliance. More differentiated assessments are also needed to identify household and individual protection needs, while recognizing capacities, skills and economic potential that can inform more targeted and sustainable support.
